The Raiders, led by third-year head coach [[Scott Nagy]], played their home games at the [[Nutter Center]] in [[Fairborn, Ohio]], as members of the [[Horizon League]]. They finished the season 21–14, 13–5 in Horizon League to be regular season co-champions with [[2018–19 Northern Kentucky Norse men's basketball team|Northern Kentucky]]. They defeated [[2018–19 IUPUI Jaguars men's basketball team|IUPUI]] and [[2018–19 Green Bay Phoenix men's basketball team|Green Bay]] to advance to the championship game of the [[2019 Horizon League men's basketball tournament|Horizon League tournament]] where they lost to Northern Kentucky. As regular season league champion, and number 1 seed in their league tournament, who failed to win their league tournament, they received an automatic bid to the [[2019 National Invitation Tournament|National Invitation Tournament]] where they lost in the first round to [[2018–19 Clemson Tigers men's basketball team|Clemson]]. ==Previous season== The [[2017–18 Wright State Raiders men's basketball team|Raiders]] finished the [[2017–18 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2017–18 season]] 25–10, 14–4 in Horizon League play to finish in second place. In the [[2018 Horizon League men's basketball tournament|Horizon League tournament]], they defeated [[2017–18 Green Bay Phoenix men's basketball team|Green Bay]], [[2017–18 Milwaukee Panthers men's basketball team|Milwaukee]], and [[2017–18 Cleveland State Vikings men's basketball team|Cleveland State]] to become Horizon League Tournament champions. This received the Horizon League's automatic bid to the [[2018 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]], where they lost to [[2017–18 Tennessee Volunteers basketball team|Tennessee]] in the first round.{{cite web |url=http://www.latimes.com/sports/la-sp-ncaa-tournament-live-updates2018-tennessee-routs-wright-state-73-47-1521141379-htmlstory.html |title=Tennessee
